content:
- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative or neutral (e.g., post-80+ peaks, model jumps to 82+ while true settles at 81+).
- Underestimate downward corrections when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -0.70 or -0.67) — model often fails to drop below recent low.
- When sentiment is mildly negative (-0.10 to -0.30), model tends to overreact upward — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% of forecasted value.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show upward trend, model often overcorrects downward — cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment was negative 3–5 days prior, model tends to overcorrect in next 3–5 days — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for each lagged negative sentiment day.
- Avoid “overshoot” after strong positive sentiment — if sentiment > 0.30, model often peaks too high — cap forecast at 1–2% below peak if sentiment > 0.30.
